1606826180.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The red arrow indicates the vertebral body (corpus vertebrae), the large, kidney-shaped anterior weight-bearing segment of the lumbar vertebra with a perforated, cribriform superior articular surface bounded by a smooth epiphysial ring.
1606826180.keyConcept: The vertebral body forms the robust, anterior weight-bearing component of each vertebra, supporting axial loads and articulating with adjacent bodies via fibrocartilaginous intervertebral discs.

422916724.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The red arrow points to the cribriform superior articular surface of the lumbar vertebral body, which is lined by a thin plate of hyaline cartilage and serves as the direct attachment site for the fibrocartilaginous intervertebral disc.
422916724.keyConcept: Intervertebral discs form secondary cartilaginous joints (symphyses) between the superior and inferior articular surfaces of adjacent vertebral bodies, providing shock absorption and tensile strength.

458564317.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The red arrow points directly to the posterior tip (apex) of the spinous process of the lumbar vertebra, which provides attachment to the supraspinous ligament.
458564317.keyConcept: The supraspinous ligament attaches to the tips of the spinous processes from vertebra C7 to the sacrum, connecting adjacent spines and limiting hyperflexion of the vertebral column.

1820578977.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The blue marker highlights the border/margin of the spinous process extending between the root and apex, which provides attachment for the interspinous ligament connecting adjacent spinous processes.
1820578977.keyConcept: Interspinous ligaments are thin membranous bands connecting adjacent spinous processes along their margins, blending posteriorly with the supraspinous ligament and anteriorly with the ligamenta flava.

1851456331.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The blue marker is placed along the anterior surface and lower border of the transverse process of the lumbar vertebra, representing the posterior (deep) slip of origin of the psoas major muscle.
1851456331.keyConcept: Psoas major arises from the anterior surfaces and lower borders of the transverse processes of all lumbar vertebrae (L1–L5), as well as from the lateral surfaces of the T12–L5 vertebral bodies and intervening intervertebral discs.

1135432685.explanation: Criteria of Identification: In this lateral view schematic of a lumbar vertebra, label 'A' indicates the lateral aspect of the vertebral body between the upper and lower margins, where the main slips and tendinous arches of the psoas major muscle arise across the constricted waist of the body.
1135432685.keyConcept: Psoas major originates via muscular slips from the margins of the lumbar vertebral bodies and discs, bridged by tendinous arches spanning across the middle of each body over the lumbar vessels.

84027891.explanation: Criteria of Identification: In this lateral view schematic of a lumbar vertebra, label 'B' designates the lumbar transverse process, corresponding to the insertion of the quadratus lumborum muscle (listed in options as 'Insertion of quadratus lamborum').
84027891.keyConcept: Quadratus lumborum inserts into the transverse processes of the upper lumbar vertebrae (L1–L4) and the inferior border of the 12th rib, stabilizing the lumbar spine and depressing the ribcage.

976115848.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Label '2' marks the broad green band covering the anterior aspect of the vertebral body, designating the anterior longitudinal ligament.
976115848.keyConcept: The anterior longitudinal ligament is a strong, broad fibrous band covering and connecting the anterior and anterolateral surfaces of the vertebral bodies and intervertebral discs, preventing hyperextension of the vertebral column.

480395565.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The blue highlighted area is positioned on the posterior surface of the vertebral body forming the anterior wall of the vertebral canal, the exact attachment site of the posterior longitudinal ligament.
480395565.keyConcept: The posterior longitudinal ligament extends along the posterior surfaces of the vertebral bodies within the vertebral canal from C2 down to the sacrum, resisting hyperflexion and helping prevent posterior disc herniation.

1490536510.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The blue marker specifically covers the apex (tip) of the transverse process of the lumbar vertebra, the definitive skeletal site where fibers of the quadratus lumborum muscle insert (listed in options as 'Insertion of quadratus lamborum').
1490536510.keyConcept: Quadratus lumborum inserts into the tips of the transverse processes of the lumbar vertebrae (L1–L4) and the lower border of the 12th rib, acting as an ipsilateral lateral flexor of the trunk.

434385648.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The blue oval lies immediately anterior to the right side of the body of the fifth lumbar vertebra (L5), corresponding to the inferior vena cava (IVC) which is formed at this anatomical level by the confluence of the right and left common iliac veins.
434385648.keyConcept: The inferior vena cava (IVC) begins on the right anterior aspect of the L5 vertebral body where the right and left common iliac veins unite behind the right common iliac artery.

602585754.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The red markers are placed on the tips of the massive, pyramidal transverse processes of the fifth lumbar vertebra (L5), which provide attachment to the stout iliolumbar ligament.
602585754.keyConcept: The iliolumbar ligament connects the transverse process of the L5 vertebra to the inner lip of the iliac crest, stabilizing the lumbosacral junction against forward translation and torsion.

100152111.explanation: Criteria of Identification: The joint indicated by label '2' (circled in yellow) is the zygapophysial (facet) joint between the inferior articular process of the superior vertebra and the superior articular process of the inferior vertebra, classified structurally as a plane synovial joint.
100152111.keyConcept: Zygapophysial (facet) joints are plane synovial joints with hyaline cartilage articular facets that guide and restrict the movements of the vertebral column.

1133876778.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Label 1 indicates the psoas minor muscle, recognized by its slender, thin muscle belly and long glistening tendon coursing down the anterior aspect of the psoas major to insert onto the pectineal line and iliopubic eminence.
1133876778.keyConcept: Psoas minor lies directly on the anterior surface of the psoas major and inserts on the iliopubic eminence; it is absent in approximately 40% of individuals.

1904885188.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Label 2 indicates the psoas major, the large, thick fusiform retroperitoneal muscle originating from the lumbar vertebrae and descending along the pelvic brim to pass deep to the inguinal ligament into the lesser trochanter.
1904885188.keyConcept: Psoas major is the chief flexor of the thigh at the hip joint and forms the lateral boundary of the pelvic brim, enclosed within the tubular psoas fascia.

476923328.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Label 3 indicates the quadratus lumborum muscle (spelled 'Quadratus lumboru' in the options), a quadrilateral muscular sheet occupying the posterior abdominal wall lateral to the psoas major between the iliac crest below and the 12th rib above.
476923328.keyConcept: Quadratus lumborum forms a major component of the posterior abdominal wall, fixes the 12th rib during forced inspiration, and produces lateral flexion of the vertebral column.

824673235.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Label 4 indicates the iliacus muscle, recognized by its broad, fan-shaped morphology lining the iliac fossa of the pelvic bone, converging with the psoas major tendon to insert into the lesser trochanter.
824673235.keyConcept: Iliacus fills the iliac fossa and joins the psoas major to form the iliopsoas muscle, the primary and most powerful flexor of the hip joint.

1650124621.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Label 1 indicates the abdominal aorta, the prominent midline retroperitoneal arterial trunk descending anterior to the lumbar vertebral column to the left of the IVC, bifurcating at the L4 level.
1650124621.keyConcept: The abdominal aorta begins at the T12 aortic hiatus of the diaphragm and terminates at the L4 vertebral level by dividing into the right and left common iliac arteries.

1723775651.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Label 2 indicates the inferior vena cava (IVC), the massive systemic venous trunk situated on the posterior abdominal wall to the right of the abdominal aorta and vertebral column.
1723775651.keyConcept: The IVC is formed at the L5 vertebral level by the confluence of the common iliac veins and ascends to pierce the central tendon of the diaphragm at the T8 level.

1411041895.explanation: Criteria of Identification: Label 3 indicates the left common iliac artery, arising from the terminal bifurcation of the abdominal aorta at the L4 level and descending inferolaterally toward the pelvic brim where it divides into internal and external iliac branches.
1411041895.keyConcept: The common iliac arteries arise from the bifurcation of the abdominal aorta at L4 and divide into the external and internal iliac arteries anterior to the sacroiliac joint.
